check: did the escape-character bug that hit one insertion contaminate any other file
origin: A here-string written in double quotes let PowerShell interpret backtick sequences as escapes, turning the literal text verifyReleaseArtifacts into a vertical tab followed by erifyReleaseArtifacts, and doing the same to 0.1.0 and fault-hit.json. Four control characters entered the report and were repaired.
whyItWasWorthSweeping: The same mechanism could have damaged any earlier here-string insertion, and a silent control character in an evidence file would be nearly invisible in review while corrupting the text.
scanValidatedByPositiveControl: A temporary file with U+000B injected was detected as one match, so the pattern finds what it looks for and the zero results are not an empty scan.
methodNote: The first pass let git quote the Chinese filenames, so some paths failed Test-Path and were skipped silently - the count of 281 checked versus 281 listed only came out right after switching to -z with core.quotepath=false. A sweep that silently skips files is the failure mode this kind of check exists to prevent.
conclusion: No other file was affected. The escape bug was confined to the one insertion where it occurred and has been repaired.
